focal_strategy: Dramatic Side-Lit Architectural Detail and Drapery
depth_strategy: Receding Perspective with Strong Atmospheric Haze
border_or_perimeter_strategy: Open Perimeter, Implied by Architectural Extension
positive_prompt: Elegant black-tie ballroom environment, Refined architectural forms bathed in dramatic side-lighting, Layered depth created with polished surfaces and subtle haze, Formal drapery shapes cascading from a high ceiling, partially obscuring distant details, Soft, warm evening lighting with strong contrast between light and shadow, Highly detailed rendering emphasizing the grandeur of the space, A sense of spaciousness and sophistication, A strictly achromatic palette of black and white, with tonal variation inside those requested neutral colours, Visual subject: An elegant black-tie ballroom environment with refined architectural forms, layered depth, formal drapery-inspired shapes and polished evening lighting, Clarified visual language: motifs: refined architectural forms, formal drapery-inspired shapes, motif structure: Motifs should be repeated in a structured and symmetrical manner, reflecting the formality of the event, atmosphere: elegant, sophisticated, celebratory, composition: symmetrical, Original brief-specific composition, coherent visual hierarchy, intentional calm negative space, balanced depth and gentle tonal modelling, Theme references are represented through brief-grounded abstract geometry, patterns, spatial structure, atmosphere and colour relationships, Architecture, environment, materials, textures and lighting are used only when supported by the brief

short_design_rationale: This direction contrasts with 'A' by utilizing an asymmetrical composition and oblique viewpoint.  The focal point is shifted to the left side of the frame with a dramatic lighting setup, and the perspective is more receding to emphasize depth. The open perimeter enhances the sense of spaciousness and suggests the ballroom extends beyond the frame. Quiet areas are placed in the upper left for titles and the lower right for programmes.
